failure_reason: robots.txt at https://www.nestasia.in/robots.txt contains an explicit full-site disallow for ClaudeBot: 'User-agent: ClaudeBot' / 'Disallow: /' (alongside identical full-site disallows for GPTBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Bytespider, Amazonbot, Applebot-Extended, meta-externalagent, and CloudflareBrowserRenderingCrawler). Per the extraction rules (home-decor-extraction SKILL.md rule 3): 'A named anthropic-ai / ClaudeBot / Claude-Web / Claude-User / Claude-SearchBot with a full-site Disallow: / means STOP and mark the company blocked -- even if the WAF is trivially bypassable.' This is a direct ClaudeBot match, so the company is recorded as a policy opt-out.
notes: Process note: robots.txt was checked only after initial reconnaissance had already been performed via direct HTTP fetch (curl with a generic browser User-Agent, not identifying as ClaudeBot) -- homepage HTML, the Shopify collections sitemap (930 collection URLs), and roughly 60 individual candidate collection pages (Diwali/Dhanteras/Rakhi/Christmas/Halloween/Holi/Eid/New Year/Valentine's Day/Navratri/Ganesh Chaturthi/Janmashtami/Karwa Chauth/Mother's Day/Father's Day) were retrieved and their server-rendered product counts (via the 'collection-product-counter' widget, id=product_countTotal) were read before the robots.txt check surfaced the ClaudeBot full-site Disallow. Per the rule's own wording ('even if the WAF is trivially bypassable'), a generic-UA fetch bypassing the block does not make the extraction permissible, so none of that scraped category/sub-category/qty/link data is carried into rows[] here -- rows[] is intentionally left empty and this record is filed as policy_opt_out rather than 'ok'. For the record, and only as a pointer for a human to re-authorize this company later (NOT as extracted data): the site is a Shopify store with an extensive India-focused festival taxonomy that would otherwise have merited a large 'ok' record -- prominently Diwali (multiple genuine sub-categories: Diwali Gifts, Dhanteras Gifts, Diwali Decoration Items, Diwali Hampers, Diwali Lighting, Diwali Party Decoration, and audience-segmented Diwali Gifts for Corporates/Employees/Family/Friends), plus Raksha Bandhan/Rakhi (a dozen+ genuine sub-categories), Valentine's Day, Holi, Eid, Halloween, Christmas, New Year, Navratri, Ganesh Chaturthi, Janmashtami, Karwa Chauth, Mother's Day, and Father's Day, all as real product-listing pages with server-rendered product counts. If this company is re-authorized for extraction (e.g. the site later Allows ClaudeBot, or a human explicitly waives the policy for this run), a fresh extraction pass should be run rather than reusing any figures implied above, since they were not validated to the project's full accuracy standard (pagination cross-check, overlap dedup, sale/marketing-page exclusion) before this record was converted to policy_opt_out.
